thread.title: Jax-based ParkerVision's patent suit against Apple, Qualcomm will remain in Florida

author: Will Robinson
title: Jax-based ParkerVision's patent suit against Apple, Qualcomm will remain in Florida
text: – Reporter, Jacksonville Business Journal Mar 12, 2018, 2:01pm EDT ParkerVision (Nasdaq: PRKR) stock spiked Monday, at one point rising 26 percent above its market opening price, on news that a federal judge denied a motion to move the case from Florida to California. ParkerVision, the Jacksonville-based developer of semiconductor technology for wireless applications, filed suit against Apple Inc. (Nasdaq: AAPL), Qualcomm (Nasdaq: QCOM), Samsung (OTC: SSNGY) and LG in 2015, claiming that the companies infringed on several of its patents. Only Apple and Qualcomm remain on the suit. In 2017, Qualcomm filed to change the venue to California, while Apple filed to dismiss due to improper venue. Judge Brian J. Davis denied both requests March 8. “We are pleased that Judge Davis has agreed with ParkerVision that the Middle District of Florida is the proper venue for this case," ParkerVision CEO Jeffrey Parker said in a statement. "We anticipate the case can now move expeditiously toward a Markman hearing, and we look forward to the court’s guidance on claim construction.” ParkerVision has a separate suit pending against Qualcomm and Samsung and another suit against LG. Though peaking at $1.11, ParkerVision stock returned close to $0.90 by time of writing, only two cents above its market opening price.
